title.en: Phase error in a coherent receiver

problem.en: In your coherent receiver, the local carrier has the right frequency but is 60° out of phase with the transmitter's carrier. What fraction of the message amplitude do you recover, what happens at 90°, and why?
problem.or: ଆପଣଙ୍କ Coherent receiver ରେ Local carrier ର Frequency ଠିକ ଅଛି, କିନ୍ତୁ Transmitter carrier ଠାରୁ Phase ରେ 60° ତଫାତ ଅଛି। Message amplitude ର କେତେ ଅଂଶ ଫେରେ, 90° ରେ କଣ ହୁଏ, ଏବଂ କାହିଁକି?

setup.en: Coherent DSB-SC receiver: multiply by the local carrier, lowpass filter, then recovery gain 2.
setup.or: Coherent DSB-SC receiver: Local carrier ସହିତ ଗୁଣନ, Lowpass filter, ତାପରେ Recovery gain 2।

given.en: Local carrier frequency equals the transmitter carrier frequency.
given.or: Local carrier frequency ଓ Transmitter carrier frequency ସମାନ।

given.en: Unit carrier amplitudes and an ideal lowpass filter.
given.or: Unit Carrier amplitude ଓ ideal Lowpass filter।

question.en: What fraction of the aligned (φ = 0°) message amplitude do you recover at 60°? What happens at 90°, and why?
question.or: 60° ରେ aligned (φ = 0°) Message amplitude ର କେତେ ଅଂଶ ଫେରେ? 90° ରେ କଣ ହୁଏ, ଏବଂ କାହିଁକି?

review.note: Machine draft. Odia not yet reviewed by a native speaker; ECE content not yet reviewed by a teacher.

sources.title: Ledger concept: Carrier mismatch and debugging
Ledger concept: Coherent demodulation and recovery gain
DSB-SC lab phase fault: Local carrier Phase pi/2 to pi

predict-60.goal: Prediction before any maths: with matched frequency and a 60° phase error, part of the message comes back (smaller than with aligned carriers, but not zero).

say.en: Let's start with a guess. At 60°, do you get all of the message back, part of it, or none?
say.or: ପ୍ରଥମେ ଗୋଟିଏ ଅନୁମାନ କରନ୍ତୁ। 60° ରେ Message ସବୁ ଫେରେ, କିଛି ଅଂଶ ଫେରେ, ନା କିଛି ବି ଫେରେ ନାହିଁ?

expect.desc: Says only part of the message comes back: smaller than with aligned carriers, but not zero. Reduced, weaker, less, partly or half all count.

misconceptions.desc: Says all of the message comes back, or that phase does not matter as long as the frequency matches.
Says nothing comes back at 60°: any phase error loses the whole message.

say.en: With the carriers lined up, you get the whole message. As their phases slip apart, does the output grow, shrink or stay the same?
say.or: Carrier ଦୁଇଟି ମେଳିଥିଲେ ପୂରା Message ମିଳେ। Phase ଅଲଗା ହେବାକୁ ଲାଗିଲେ Output ବଢ଼େ, କମେ, ନା ସମାନ ରହେ?

say.en: Phase decides how well the two carriers line up. At 60° they line up only partly.
say.or: Carrier ଦୁଇଟିର ମେଳ କେତେ ଭଲ, ତାହା Phase ସ୍ଥିର କରେ। 60° ରେ ମେଳ ଆଂଶିକ।

say.en: The output is the message times a factor that depends on φ. At 0° that factor is 1; watch what happens at 60°.
say.or: Output ହେଉଛି Message × ଏକ Factor, ଯାହା φ ଉପରେ ନିର୍ଭର କରେ। 0° ରେ ଏହି Factor 1; 60° ରେ ଏହା କଣ ହୁଏ ଦେଖନ୍ତୁ।

say.en: Part of it. The recovered trace is smaller than the aligned one, but it is not zero.
say.or: କିଛି ଅଂଶ ଫେରେ। Recovered trace aligned trace ଠାରୁ ଛୋଟ, କିନ୍ତୁ ଶୂନ୍ୟ ନୁହେଁ।

chips.text: All of it, because the frequency matches.
Part of it. It gets smaller, but not zero.
None of it. Out of phase means the message is lost.

show-phase-matters.goal: Counter 'only frequency matters': the frequency stays matched, φ moves to 60°, and the recovered trace shrinks against the aligned trace.

say.en: Here the frequency matches exactly, and only the phase moved to 60°. Look: the recovered trace is smaller than the aligned one.
say.or: ଏଠାରେ Frequency ପୂରା ମେଳୁଛି, କେବଳ Phase 60° କୁ ଘୁଞ୍ଚିଛି। ଦେଖନ୍ତୁ: Recovered trace aligned trace ଠାରୁ ଛୋଟ।

show-part-survives.goal: Counter 'any phase error loses everything': at 60° the recovered trace is smaller but clearly not zero.

say.en: At 60° the recovered trace is smaller, but it is still there. Part of the message survives.
say.or: 60° ରେ Recovered trace ଛୋଟ ହୁଏ, କିନ୍ତୁ ଏବେ ବି ଅଛି। Message ର କିଛି ଅଂଶ ରହିଯାଏ।

why-cos.goal: Mechanism: multiplying by the local carrier and lowpass filtering leaves m(t) scaled by cos φ (½ m(t) cos φ before the recovery gain of 2, m(t) cos φ after it).

say.en: Your receiver multiplies by the local carrier, then lowpass filters. How does the phase error φ change m(t) at the output?
say.or: Receiver ପ୍ରଥମେ Local carrier ସହିତ ଗୁଣନ କରେ, ତାପରେ Lowpass filter କରେ। Phase error φ ଯୋଗୁଁ Output ରେ m(t) କିପରି ବଦଳେ?

expect.desc: Says m(t) is multiplied or scaled by cos φ: the output is m(t) cos φ after the recovery gain, or ½ m(t) cos φ before it, or the amplitude follows cos φ.
Gives only the aligned-carrier result: the product leaves m(t)/2 and the gain of 2 restores m(t). No mention of φ or cos φ.

misconceptions.desc: Says the phase error cancels in the product, or the lowpass filter or the gain removes it, so the output is still m(t).

say.en: Write the carriers as cos(ωt) and cos(ωt + φ). What do you get when you multiply them?
say.or: Carrier ଦୁଇଟିକୁ cos(ωt) ଓ cos(ωt + φ) ଭାବରେ ଲେଖନ୍ତୁ। ଦୁହିଁଙ୍କୁ ଗୁଣନ କଲେ କଣ ମିଳେ?

say.en: Use cos A cos B = ½[cos(A − B) + cos(A + B)]. The lowpass filter keeps only the low-frequency part.
say.or: cos A cos B = ½[cos(A − B) + cos(A + B)] ବ୍ୟବହାର କରନ୍ତୁ। Lowpass filter କେବଳ କମ Frequency ଅଂଶ ରଖେ।

say.en: The low-frequency part is ½ m(t) cos φ. The recovery gain of 2 makes it m(t) cos φ.
say.or: ସେହି କମ Frequency ଅଂଶଟି ହେଉଛି ½ m(t) cos φ। Recovery gain 2 ତାକୁ m(t) cos φ କରେ।

say.en: The phase error scales m(t) by cos φ. The output is m(t) cos φ.
say.or: Phase error ଯୋଗୁଁ m(t) ର Amplitude cos φ ଗୁଣ ହୁଏ। Output ହେଉଛି m(t) cos φ।

chips.text: It scales m(t) by cos φ, so the output is m(t) cos φ.
Nothing changes. The lowpass filter removes the phase error, so I still get m(t).
The product gives m(t)/2, and the gain of 2 brings it back to m(t).

show-cos-factor.goal: Show where cos φ comes from: after the lowpass filter ½ m(t) cos φ is left, the recovery gain of 2 gives m(t) cos φ, and neither the filter nor the gain removes cos φ.

say.en: After the lowpass filter, ½ m(t) cos φ is left, and the recovery gain of 2 makes it m(t) cos φ. Neither one removes the cos φ.
say.or: Lowpass filter ପରେ ½ m(t) cos φ ରହେ, ଆଉ Recovery gain 2 ତାକୁ m(t) cos φ କରେ। Filter ବା Gain, କେଉଁଟି ବି cos φ କୁ ହଟାଏ ନାହିଁ।

calc-60.goal: Calculation: cos 60° = 0.5, so the output is half of the aligned amplitude.

say.en: Use that factor. At 60°, what fraction of the aligned amplitude comes out?
say.or: ସେହି Factor ବ୍ୟବହାର କରନ୍ତୁ। 60° ରେ aligned Amplitude ର କେତେ ଅଂଶ Output ରେ ମିଳେ?

expect.desc: Gives 0.5, one half or 50% of the aligned amplitude, from cos 60° = 0.5.

misconceptions.desc: Gives a value from treating 60 as radians, such as about −0.95 (calculator in radian mode), or otherwise mixes up degrees and radians.

say.en: Which function of φ did we find? Put φ = 60° into it.
say.or: ଆମେ φ ର କେଉଁ Function ପାଇଲେ? ସେଥିରେ φ = 60° ରଖନ୍ତୁ।

say.en: Keep your calculator in degree mode, or use 60° = π/3 rad. Cosine does not fall in a straight line with the angle.
say.or: Calculator କୁ Degree mode ରେ ରଖନ୍ତୁ, କିମ୍ବା 60° = π/3 rad ନିଅନ୍ତୁ। Angle ବଢ଼ିଲେ Cosine ସିଧା ରେଖାରେ କମେ ନାହିଁ।

say.en: In degrees, cos 60° = cos(π/3) = 0.5. So the output is 0.5 × m(t).
say.or: Degree ରେ cos 60° = cos(π/3) = 0.5। ତେଣୁ Output = 0.5 × m(t)।

say.en: Half. At 60° you recover half of the aligned amplitude.
say.or: ଅଧା। 60° ରେ aligned Amplitude ର ଅଧା ଫେରେ।

chips.text: cos 60° is 0.5, so half of the aligned amplitude.
My calculator says cos 60 is about −0.95.

show-angle-units.goal: Fix the unit slip: 60° is π/3 rad, not 60 rad, and cos 60° = 0.5. Reveal the readout at 60°.

say.en: Check the angle unit: 60° is π/3 radians, not 60 radians. So cos 60° = cos(π/3) = 0.5, and half comes out.
say.or: Angle ର Unit ଦେଖନ୍ତୁ: 60° ମାନେ π/3 radian, 60 radian ନୁହେଁ। ତେଣୁ cos 60° = cos(π/3) = 0.5, ଆଉ ଅଧା ଫେରେ।

predict-90.goal: Extend: at φ = 90°, cos 90° = 0, so the ideal message component vanishes. The student says what comes out and why.

say.en: Now make the phase error 90°. What comes out, and why?
say.or: ଏବେ Phase error 90° କରନ୍ତୁ। Output ରେ କଣ ମିଳେ, ଆଉ କାହିଁକି?

expect.desc: Says nothing comes out, or only a small residual ripple, because cos 90° = 0: the ideal message component vanishes.

misconceptions.desc: Says the message flips or inverts because 90° is half a cycle (π), or gives cos of 90 radians (about −0.45).
Says the full message still comes out because the frequency matches.

say.en: Use the same factor. What is cos 90°?
say.or: ସେହି Factor ବ୍ୟବହାର କରନ୍ତୁ। cos 90° କେତେ?

say.en: 90° is a quarter cycle, π/2 rad, not a half cycle. Where is a cosine wave a quarter cycle along?
say.or: 90° ମାନେ quarter cycle, ଅର୍ଥାତ୍ π/2 rad; ଏହା half cycle ନୁହେଁ। Quarter cycle ପରେ Cosine wave କେଉଁଠି ଥାଏ?

say.en: At 90°, cos 90° = 0, so the output is m(t) × 0.
say.or: 90° ରେ cos 90° = 0, ତେଣୁ Output = m(t) × 0।

say.en: Nothing comes out: the ideal message component vanishes at 90°. A real lowpass filter can leave a little ripple.
say.or: Output ରେ କିଛି ମିଳେ ନାହିଁ: 90° ରେ ideal Message ଅଂଶ ଶୂନ୍ୟ ହୁଏ। ବାସ୍ତବ Lowpass filter ପାଇଁ ଟିକିଏ Ripple ରହିପାରେ।

chips.text: Nothing comes out, because cos 90° is 0.
The message flips upside down, because 90° is half a cycle.
I still get the full message, because the frequency matches.

show-90.goal: Reveal 90°: the ideal recovered trace goes flat because cos 90° = 0. Name 90° as a quarter cycle (π/2 rad) and give the finite-filter residual caveat (ledger M-AM-08).

say.en: At 90°, a quarter cycle, cos 90° = 0, so the ideal message vanishes. A real lowpass filter can still leave a little ripple.
say.or: 90° ରେ, ଅର୍ଥାତ୍ quarter cycle ରେ, cos 90° = 0, ତେଣୁ ideal Message ଶୂନ୍ୟ ହୁଏ। ବାସ୍ତବ Lowpass filter ପାଇଁ ତଥାପି ଟିକିଏ Ripple ରହିପାରେ।

explain-english.goal: Articulation: in English, in one or two sentences, the student explains why the output is m(t) cos φ and what that gives at 60° and 90°, using course terms (local carrier or local oscillator, lowpass filter, phase error).

say.en: Last step: explain it to your lab partner in English, in one or two sentences. Try to use local carrier, lowpass filter and phase error.
say.or: ଶେଷ ପଦକ୍ଷେପ: ଆପଣଙ୍କ Lab partner କୁ ଇଂରାଜୀରେ ଗୋଟିଏ ବା ଦୁଇଟି ବାକ୍ୟରେ ବୁଝାନ୍ତୁ। Local carrier, Lowpass filter ଓ Phase error ଶବ୍ଦ ବ୍ୟବହାର କରିବାକୁ ଚେଷ୍ଟା କରନ୍ତୁ।

expect.desc: Explains in English: the out-of-phase local carrier leaves m(t) cos φ after the product and the lowpass filter, so 60° gives half and 90° gives nothing (ideally). Gives both the reason and the result, with at least two course terms.
Explains only part: the result without the reason, or the reason without the result; or uses few course terms; or answers mostly in Odia with English terms.

say.en: Start with the cause: “The local carrier is 60° out of phase, so …”. What happens to the output?
say.or: କାରଣରୁ ଆରମ୍ଭ କରନ୍ତୁ: “The local carrier is 60° out of phase, so …”। Output ରେ କଣ ହୁଏ?

say.en: Add the rule and the numbers: “… the output is m(t) times …, so at 60° … and at 90° …”.
say.or: Rule ଓ ସଂଖ୍ୟା ଯୋଡ଼ନ୍ତୁ: “… the output is m(t) times …, so at 60° … and at 90° …”।

say.en: Fill the blanks: “Because of the phase error, the receiver output is m(t) cos φ, so 60° gives ___ and 90° gives ___.”
say.or: ଖାଲି ସ୍ଥାନ ପୂରଣ କରନ୍ତୁ: “Because of the phase error, the receiver output is m(t) cos φ, so 60° gives ___ and 90° gives ___.”

say.en: One way to say it: “Because the local carrier is out of phase, the receiver output is m(t) cos φ, so 60° gives half and 90° gives nothing.” Now say it in your own words.
say.or: ଏହିପରି କହିପାରିବେ: “Because the local carrier is out of phase, the receiver output is m(t) cos φ, so 60° gives half and 90° gives nothing.” ଏବେ ନିଜ ଶବ୍ଦରେ ଇଂରାଜୀରେ କୁହନ୍ତୁ।

chips.text: Can you give me a sentence starter?
The local carrier is out of phase, so the output is m(t) cos φ: half at 60° and nothing at 90°.

conclusion.goal: Close with the model explanation, both results and the finite-filter caveat, then point to the lab's 90° phase-fault step (CP-DSB-11).

say.en: Here is the whole idea: after the local carrier, the lowpass filter and the recovery gain, the output is m(t) cos φ. So 60° gives half the amplitude, and 90° gives none.
say.or: ପୂରା କଥାଟି ଏହା: Local carrier ସହିତ ଗୁଣନ, Lowpass filter ଓ Recovery gain ପରେ Output ହେଉଛି m(t) cos φ। ତେଣୁ 60° ରେ ଅଧା Amplitude ମିଳେ, ଆଉ 90° ରେ କିଛି ମିଳେ ନାହିଁ।

summary.en: Multiplying by the local carrier, lowpass filtering and the recovery gain of 2 leave m(t) cos φ. At 60° you keep half the amplitude (cos 60° = 0.5); at 90° the ideal message vanishes (cos 90° = 0), though a real filter can leave a little ripple. In English: “Because the local carrier is out of phase, the receiver output is m(t) cos φ, so 60° gives half and 90° gives nothing.” Next: try the 90° receiver phase fault in the lab.
summary.or: Local carrier ସହିତ ଗୁଣନ, Lowpass filter ଓ Recovery gain 2 ପରେ m(t) cos φ ରହେ। 60° ରେ ଅଧା Amplitude ରହେ (cos 60° = 0.5); 90° ରେ ideal Message ଶୂନ୍ୟ ହୁଏ (cos 90° = 0), ତଥାପି ବାସ୍ତବ Filter ପାଇଁ ଟିକିଏ Ripple ରହିପାରେ। ଇଂରାଜୀରେ: “Because the local carrier is out of phase, the receiver output is m(t) cos φ, so 60° gives half and 90° gives nothing.” ପରବର୍ତ୍ତୀ ପଦକ୍ଷେପ: Lab ରେ 90-degree Receiver phase fault ପରୀକ୍ଷା କରନ୍ତୁ।

why.en: Try the phase fault in the lab: shift the local carrier phase and watch the recovered message shrink.
Revisit coherent demodulation: why the local carrier must match the transmitter carrier in phase as well as frequency.
Revisit angles and phase: a quarter cycle is 90 degrees, or pi/2 radians.
